# BigQuery Conversational Analytics: Data Agent Kit, Google ADK and MCP Review


BigQuery conversational analytics reviewed: Gemini data agents, Google ADK, Data Agent Kit and MCP, how they work, their limits, and the open source alternative.


25 November 2026


By Claire Gouze


Founder @ nao


Google now ships an AI agent for every layer of BigQuery. Each one keeps your data team inside Google's walls.


**BigQuery conversational analytics** is Google's answer to "chat with your data": business users ask questions in plain English to **Gemini data agents** and get text, tables and charts. Around it, Google offers **Google ADK** to build custom agents, **Data Agent Kit** with **MCP tools** for coding agents, and **Gemini Enterprise** . Three problems come back with every option: **the context is restricted** to what Google's catalog accepts, **the models are Gemini's** in the ready-made products, and **the custom options leave you to build your own UI** . None of them gives your data team a way to test answers before people act on them. **nao** is the open source alternative: an analytics agent your data team builds, tests and monitors on BigQuery and any other warehouse.


This review is based on Google's release notes and on data teams who evaluated Gemini against nao.


## BigQuery conversational analytics: Google's four ways to build a data agent


Google's[What's new with Google Data Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/data-analytics/whats-new-with-google-data-cloud) page describes four building blocks:


- **Conversational analytics in BigQuery** : data agents powered by Gemini, in multi-turn conversations inside BigQuery. Answers are text, tables and charts you can export to CSV or PDF. Gemini only, BigQuery only.
- **The Conversational Analytics API** : the same agent as an API. The interface your business users will see is yours to build.
- **Google ADK** : the **Agent Development Kit** , a framework to code custom agents in Python on Gemini and Vertex AI. You get an agent loop: the UI, the context, the tests and the monitoring are yours to build.
- **Data Agent Kit** : free MCP tools and Google-written skills that connect more than 15 Google Data Cloud services to coding agents in VS Code, Cursor, Claude Code and Codex. Built for developers in an IDE, not for business users.
- **Gemini Enterprise** and **Data Cloud connectors in Gemini** (preview): questions on BigQuery, Looker, Spanner, AlloyDB and Cloud SQL from Google Docs, Gmail and Slides. Gemini only.


All of them read the same context: **Knowledge Catalog** . It accepts metadata, semantic models (LookML, dbt MetricFlow and a few others), golden queries and a glossary. That is the whole menu. Your markdown business rules, your dbt docs as written, your internal wiki, your own skills: there is no place for them unless you rewrite them into Google's formats.


## Context: restrictive and written by hand


Andrei Fateev's[hands-on guide](https://medium.com/@andrei_15463/part-2b-hands-on-building-a-semantic-context-layer-with-knowledge-catalog-bigquery-property-ef18fcdacada) to Knowledge Catalog splits the work into three tiers:


1. **Easy, automated** : technical metadata, data profiling and Gemini Data Insights.
2. **Medium** : property and semantic graph DDL, and curated **golden queries** .
3. **Hard** : a governed **business glossary** , agreed across stakeholders.


Only the first tier is automatic, and it is the one that matters least. Golden queries and the glossary, where answer quality is decided, are written by hand, in Google's formats, and only serve Google's agents. Compare that with what made the difference in[our own study](https://getnao.io/blog/improve-analytics-agent-reliability-steps/) : date rules, dbt docs and data model fixes, none of which fit in a glossary.


## BigQuery MCP: what Data Agent Kit does


Data Agent Kit does not give business users anything. Its MCP tools let a coding agent inspect schemas, run queries, read job logs and manage resources ([TechCEO Daily](https://www.techceodaily.com/saas/google-data-agent-kit-ga-coding-agents) ). Agents run as the user or a service account, so permissions are on you: Code & Chain[warns](https://www.codeandchain.com/en/articles/2026-11-21/article-727e5cb1c212) that data teams must revisit IAM roles so agents don't get overly broad query rights.


The kit is free; every query your agents run is billed at standard BigQuery prices.


## BigQuery conversational analytics vs nao


The five criteria we use when a data team compares the two:


Gemini (BigQuery, ADK, Gemini Enterprise) nao


LLM Gemini in BigQuery and Gemini Enterprise; Vertex AI models with ADK **Bring your own key** : Claude, GPT, Gemini, Mistral, Bedrock, Ollama


Context **Restricted** to Knowledge Catalog: metadata, golden queries, glossary, written by hand **Flexible file system** , generated automatically by` nao sync` , edited in Git


Interface Chat with charts in BigQuery; **build your own UI** with the API or ADK Chat plus reporting: stories, dashboards, Slack, Teams, Claude through the nao MCP


Evaluation **None**` nao test` on your own questions, in CI


Observability Latency, adoption and cost **Chats Replay** of every answer, user feedback and **context recommendations**


License Proprietary **Open source, Apache 2.0**


## BigQuery conversational analytics limitations


1. **Nobody tests the answers.** Google's observability for data agents tracks adoption, latency and cost, not whether answers are right. We found no test suite that checks answers against reference SQL before a release.
2. **The context is restricted.** Only what Knowledge Catalog accepts reaches the agent: metadata, semantic models, golden queries, a glossary. Your markdown rules, dbt docs and custom skills have to be rewritten into those formats, by hand.
3. **You are limited to Gemini.** Conversational analytics in BigQuery and Gemini Enterprise run on Gemini. If Claude or GPT answers your questions better, you can't switch the model of the ready-made products.
4. **You build your own UI.** The ready-made agent lives in the BigQuery console, where business users don't go. To put it in Slack, Teams or your own app, you code the interface on the Conversational Analytics API or ADK, then maintain it.


## Should you build your analytics agent on BigQuery and Google ADK?


Not if your data team wants to own it. It is lock-in by design:


- **Your context is tied to Google Cloud.** Move part of your data to another warehouse and the agent's context does not follow.
- **Your models are Google's.** Gemini in the ready-made products, Vertex AI with ADK, at Google's rates.
- **ADK is a framework, not a product.** You still build the agent, the UI, the evaluation and the monitoring yourself, and your data team becomes a software team.


## nao: the open source alternative on BigQuery


**nao is open source (Apache 2.0).** Self-host it or run it on nao Cloud, bring your own LLM, read every line of the agent. It runs on BigQuery as a first-class warehouse, and on Snowflake, Databricks, Postgres and the rest of your stack.


### How to set up nao on BigQuery


1. ` pip install nao-core` ,` nao init` , and pick **BigQuery** ([database docs](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-builder/databases) ). Authenticate with a service account (required on nao Cloud) or Application Default Credentials.
2. Set` max_query_size` in GB: nao dry runs every query and stops the ones that would scan more. Use` exclude_columns` to keep sensitive columns away from the agent.
3. ` nao sync` generates the context as files: table and column descriptions, profiling, AI summaries and query history. Add your[dbt repo](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-builder/repos) and your rules in` RULES.md` , following our[context engineering guide](https://getnao.io/blog/how-to-do-context-engineering-for-data-teams/) .


1. Write 20 to 40 real questions with their reference SQL and run[nao test](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-engineering/evaluation) . A test passes only when the agent's data matches your SQL.


1. Deploy in[Slack](https://getnao.io/blog/setup-ai-analytics-slack-bot-open-source/) , Teams or Claude through the[nao MCP](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-mcp/) , and share answers as[stories](https://getnao.io/blog/how-to-turn-chat-with-data-into-shareable-stories/) . Watch real usage in Chats Replay, apply[context recommendations](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-context-recommendations/) , and click **Save as test** on any wrong answer.
